header:
Date: 2029-03-06
Time: 15:00 PT / 18:00 ET
Duration: 58 mins
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE); Samir Khatri (Redwood Partnerships); Ellen Cho (Voyant Head of Partnerships); Ravi Menon (Voyant CTO); Luca Bianchi (Voyant Platform Eng); Tara Singh (Voyant Security)
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Voyant Nimbus to scope reseller integration and technical onramp. High-level alignment on use cases (managed inference for Voyant customers + white-labeled offering), integration modes (hosted API vs dedicated pools vs private VPC), security/compliance needs, and pilot next steps. Action items assigned for network, compliance docs, and an SE-led latency baseline.
topics: Integration options: hosted API, dedicated capacity, private deployment (VPC/on-prem)
Network architecture and VPC peering requirements
SLA/SL0 expectations and pricing model for reseller
Security: SOC 2, KMS/HSM, audit logs, data residency
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, then we're gonna frame out what a reseller onramp might look like.
[00:17] Ellen (Voyant): Hi all, Ellen here, we run partner ops at Voyant Nimbus. Excited to see how Redwood could fit into our managed offering.
[00:25] Ravi (Voyant): Hey, Ravi here. CTO. We care about throughput, ops cost, and being able to white-label endpoints.
[00:33] Diego (Redwood): Great. I'll cover some of the technical options, latency profiles, routing. Samir will talk GTM a bit.
[00:39] Samir (Redwood): hi hi, quick note on commercial models after tech.
[00:45] [00:45] Luca (Voyant): quick one, is this more hosted api or fully private? we have a mix of customers.
[00:52] Maya: good Q. We support three primary modes: Hosted API for fast time-to-market; Dedicated GPU pools for reserved throughput and isolation; Private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated customers. Most partners start with hosted or dedicated depending on volume.
[01:12] Tara (Voyant): from security side we need KMS integration, audit logs, and SOC2 evidence. also, data residency for EU customers.
[01:24] Diego: totally. We integrate with customer KMS, support HSM-backed keys for Private, and we emit audit logs per-token and per-request in the Console. SOC2 is available and we can share the report under NDA.
[01:38] Ellen: perfect, you'll send that. also licensing: do you allow resale at markup, and is there a partner discount?
[01:47] Maya: yes, we have a reseller pricing tier — Samir can share the tiered discount table. For pilots we often provide credits to reduce friction.
[01:56] Samir: i'll follow up on partner T&Cs and margins, short note: there's also co-selling credits for first 6 months.
[02:06] [02:06] Ravi: on the technical side — what are typical latency numbers for hosted vs dedicated? some of our customers are latency-sensitive for chat applications.
[02:17] Diego: good one — hosted latencies for our most optimized text-gen model at 512 tokens typically p50 ~ 70-120ms depending on region; p95 ~ 200-400ms. Dedicated pools improve tail latency and throughput — expect p95 under 200ms for tuned configs, larger models will be higher. caveat: quantization and kernel selection matter.
[02:45] Luca: when you say dedicated pools, do you support bursting to hosted when capacity saturated? we want graceful degradation.
[02:54] Diego: yes, smart routing supports fallback to compatible model variants in hosted when dedicated is full — policy driven. You can prefer latency or cost in the routing policy.
[03:06] [03:06] Tara: what about KV cache and prefix caching — we need to ensure cost control for repeated queries.
[03:14] Diego: we have automatic prefix caching and KV cache for chat workloads — reduces token costs and latency for repeated contexts. There are cache invalidation hooks you can call.
[03:26] Ellen: nice. for the reseller flow how do calls authenticate — do we create per-customer API keys or do you support SSO and token broker?
[03:36] Maya: both. Typical reseller pattern: Voyant owns parent account and we support per-sub-account API keys, and there's a managed SSO path for end customers. For high security, your engineers can run Private with a managed control plane and self-hosted runtime.
[03:50] Ravi: network — we need peering and egress IPs if we do VPC. can you document the ranges?
[03:57] Diego: yes, we'll provide CIDR ranges and peering guides. For Private we support both Transit Gateway and VPC peering. we'll send a checklist.
[04:08] [04:08] Luca: for the pilot, can you run a synthetic baseline with 1k qps to show tail latencies?
[04:15] Diego: yes, we can spin up a dedicated pool and run a baseline. need to verify model and token length, and we should align on region.
[04:25] Maya: target region for pilot?
[04:28] Ellen: EU + US, start in us-west then eu-west.
[04:31] Diego: noted.
[04:34] [04:34] Ravi: on billing, how does metering work if Voyant is reselling? do we get consolidated invoices?
[04:42] Samir: resellers can get consolidated billing or we can do per-customer invoicing via our partner portal. There are reporting APIs for usage.
[04:51] Tara: audit logs and retention — length of logs available? com requirement is 1 year.
[04:57] Diego: logs retention defaults to 90 days; extended retention is an add-on we can enable up to multi-year for enterprise. retention settings per-account in Console.
[05:08] [05:08] Ellen: any blockers for going to pilot?
[05:12] Maya: main items: network ranges, compliance docs, and a quick commercial note. we can do pilot while NDA/contract finishes.
[05:20] Luca: for private deployment, do you ship an on-prem bundle or is it containerized?
[05:27] Diego: it's containerized with Helm charts and supports air-gapped installs; we also offer an appliance option with partner integrators for larger deployments. note: on-prem path takes longer for onboarding.
[05:41] Ravi: curious about observability — do we get token-level cost breakdowns? we need to show customers exact spend per model/route.
[05:50] Diego: yes, Console has token-level breakdown, route-level dashboards, tracing hooks. you can plug in your datadog or prometheus for metrics ingestion.
[06:02] [06:02] Ellen: any limitations on model catalog for resellers? we'd like to offer a subset to our customers.
[06:10] Maya: you can curate the catalog per sub-account and pin model versions. You can also restrict by compute tier.
[06:18] Tara: KMS. we'll require HSM backed keys for EU regulated customers.
[06:24] Diego: supported. for Private we support KMS/HSM integrations and customer-managed keys. point in the notes: ensure key rotation policies align.
[06:35] [06:35] Ellen: do you integrate with partner billing systems via APIs? we want automated invoicing.
[06:41] Samir: there are billing APIs; we can also do SFTP/EDI batch reports for larger partners.
[06:49] Luca: any example latency numbers for embeddings? many of our customers use embeddings for semantic search.
[06:56] Diego: embeddings are typically cheaper and lower latency. p50 under 30ms in optimized regions, p95 under 120ms, but this depends on dimension and vector post-processing.
[07:08] [07:08] Ravi: what's the typical quantization impact on latency/quality if we go to int8?
[07:15] Diego: quantization to int8 reduces memory footprint ~2-4x and can cut latency by 20-40% for certain kernels. quality regressions are model-dependent — we recommend A/B evals run with Redwood Optimize to track regression.
[07:30] Ellen: can you white-label the Console? we want partners to feel it's our product.
[07:36] Samir: partial white-labeling is supported — custom logos, domain, and partner onboarding flows. Deep white-labeling for large resellers is possible as a professional services engagement.
[07:49] [07:49] Tara: on compliance, we need PCI scope implications when customers pass payment tokens to prompts. any guidance?
[07:58] Diego: short answer: avoid sending raw card numbers. we also recommend tokenizing PII on client side and using redaction hooks; private deployments can keep that data from crossing public clouds. We'll share guidance docs.
[08:15] Ellen: do you have marketplace integrations, e.g., AWS marketplace?
[08:20] Maya: yes, Redwood has marketplace listings and partner programs. that can be part of GTM.
[08:26] [08:26] Ravi: SLA specifics — uptime numbers and credits?
[08:33] Samir: Dedicated contracts come with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. Hosted has best-effort SLAs, but we can offer enterprise SLA in reseller agreements. we'll send standard SLA language.
[08:46] Luca: technical deep dive — how do you handle KV cache sharding across GPUs?
[08:52] Diego: cache is sharded by session ID and routed to the serving instance maintaining that KV. For scale we replicate hot keys across nodes and have eviction policies. it's tunable per deployment.
[09:06] [09:06] Ellen: customers will ask about data deletion and retention for GDPR. what's the flow?
[09:13] Diego: we support deletion APIs, and private deployments can ensure data never leaves their cloud. For hosted, data retention and deletion controls are available via Console and audit logs are generated. We'll provide a GDPR playbook.
[09:29] Tara: we need a security review timeline — typically 2-4 weeks?
[09:34] Maya: depends on scope; for pilot often 2 weeks if Voyager supplies docs quickly. full enterprise white-label plus private deployment is longer.
[09:44] [09:44] Ravi: for pilot success criteria — propose: (1) sustained 500 qps for 30 minutes with <= 250ms p95, (2) integration of billing/reporting APIs, (3) completed security questionnaire.
[09:57] Maya: good start, we'll formalize criteria in a doc and share.
[10:04] Samir: on co-selling: Voyant will get joint GTM assets from Redwood. let's coordinate collateral.
[10:12] Ellen: we'll need a partner briefing deck for sales enablement.
[10:16] Samir: we'll provide a starter deck.
[10:20] [10:20] Luca: any constraints on model weights licensing if we white-label? some open models have licensing caveats.
[10:28] Diego: licensing varies per model. Redwood curates a model catalog and flags license constraints; we'll help choose models suitable for commercial resale.
[10:37] Tara: do you have penetration test or external vuln reports?
[10:42] Maya: yes, we can share high level summaries; full reports under NDA.
[10:47] [10:47] Ellen: okay, next steps?
[10:51] Maya: action items: Diego to send integration checklist and CIDR ranges; Tara to send compliance questionnaire; Samir to send partner pricing; Voyant to decide pilot region and target customers.
[11:03] Ravi: can we schedule pilot kickoff for week of March 18th?
[11:07] Maya: sounds good. We'll Doodle.
[11:11] [11:11] Diego: i'll set up a follow-up tech session to nail down the benchmark parameters (model, token lengths, payload sizes).
[11:17] Ellen: thanks everyone, excited to move forward.
[11:20] Maya: thanks all, talk soon.
[11:24] [11:24] (meeting end)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings — Voyant sometimes transcribed as "Voyager" in the raw export; some product names were auto-corrected. Speaker labels were mostly accurate but there are a few short overlaps and crosstalk instances.
